overall_summary: FACTVERSE is experiencing a massive surge in performance when focusing on extreme exoplanets, cosmic anomalies, and bizarre planetary weather (e.g., burning ice, supersonic rubies, and coal-dark worlds). Conversely, cognitive psychology and basic animal trivia are severely underperforming, indicating that the audience craves high-concept, visually spectacular cosmic mysteries over abstract human biology or common animal facts.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice' reached 1,055 views, 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' achieved 1,019 views, and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' reached 721 views.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on bizarre planetary conditions, focusing on extreme temperatures, strange rain (rubies, iron, glass), and visually striking cosmic anomalies.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into This $26 Nonillion Diamond Planet?' secured 339 views and 23 likes, showing high engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Frame astronomical facts as hypothetical, high-stakes first-person explorations to increase viewer immersion and retention.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' failed to gain traction across multiple uploads (max 53 views), and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' got only 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Phase out abstract cognitive psychology topics unless they can be framed with a high-stakes sci-fi or survival hook.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever' got 69 views, and 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' plateaued at 183 views.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid basic, widely known animal facts. Pivot animal content toward cinematic survival stories or extreme evolutionary mysteries.
